entries.expected_signal: JSON output with parse_config_h results for synthetic pyconfig.h input
entries.reachability_signal: parse_config_h returns dict with 14 entries covering quoted and unquoted #define values

contracts.detail: 8 out of 14 config values changed format (surrounding double-quotes stripped). 6 integer values unchanged. This is the intended behavior change to fix double-quoting issue in gh-150208.

behavior_differences.before: String config values returned with surrounding double-quotes (e.g., '"blake2,sha256"')
behavior_differences.after: String config values returned without surrounding double-quotes (e.g., 'blake2,sha256')
behavior_differences.evidence: Before: 8 quoted string values. After: 0 quoted string values. All 3 patch lines (440, 449, 450) confirmed executed via coverage.

notes: All 3 added lines in parse_config_h covered at 100%
Contract breach is intentional — fixes double-quoting bug
Downstream tools (pip, setuptools, virtualenv) may need updates if they expect quoted format

conclusion.rationale: The patch intentionally changes the output format of parse_config_h (and transitively get_config_vars/get_config_var). String-type #define values from pyconfig.h no longer include surrounding double-quotes. This fixes a bug where sysconfigdata variables were double-quoted. Although this is a bug fix, it is a backward-incompatible change for any code that depends on the old quoted-string format. All 3 patch lines achieved 100% coverage in testing.
recommended_actions: Notify downstream projects (pip, setuptools, virtualenv, distlib) about the format change
Update any Python packaging tools that parse sysconfig output expecting quoted strings
Verify that the existing CPython test suite passes with this change
Consider documenting this change in the Python release notes as a behavior change in sysconfig
